Raymond III was the Count of Tripoli from 1147 to 1177 and one of the most prominent leaders of the Crusader states He played a key role in the political and military history of the region during his reign

He was the son of Raymond II and Helena of Jerusalem and succeeded his father at a young age Raymond III was known for his military prowess and his attempts to expand the borders of the County of Tripoli

*Raymond III was a skilled military leader who led several campaigns against the Muslim forces in the region including the Siege of Ascalon in 1153 and the Battle of Inab in 1154*

He was also involved in the politics of the Kingdom of Jerusalem and supported the claims of Amalric I to the throne Raymond III married Agnes of Courtenay but the marriage was annulled due to their close family relationship

Raymond III was captured by Nur ad-Din during the Battle of Inab in 1154 and held prisoner for several years He was released in 1157 and returned to Tripoli where he continued to rule until his death in 1177

*The County of Tripoli under Raymond III experienced a period of relative peace and stability despite the ongoing conflicts with Muslim forces in the region*

Raymond III died in 1177 without an heir and the County of Tripoli was inherited by his nephew Hugh III of Cyprus Raymond III is remembered as one of the most important figures in the history of the Crusader states

*Raymond III played a crucial role in the Second Crusade and was a key ally of the Kingdom of Jerusalem in the region*
